h2: Water Pumps & Filters Bali – Keeping Your Villa Supplied
intro: If your villa's pressure pump is short-cycling or the rooftop tank never fills, you're not alone — Water Pumps & Filters Bali issues are among the most common requests I receive across Canggu, Uluwatu and Ubud. Whether it's a slightly brackish well near Jimbaran or a gravity-fed setup on the Bukit, I trace the fault, swap worn components and get steady flow back to every tap.

sections.text: A pressure switch stuck in the 'on' position makes the pump cycle every few seconds, burning out the motor within weeks. In coastal stretches like Seminyak and Sanur, wells often pull slightly brackish water that corrodes impellers faster than expected. On the Bukit — Uluwatu, Bingin, Pererenan — gravity-fed tanks mean any blockage in the line or a cracked float valve leaves you with no water upstairs. Pinpointing which of these is happening saves hours of guesswork.

sections.h3: What a Pump & Filter Service Covers
sections.text: I begin at the source: checking the well pump's amperage draw, testing the pressure-switch cut-in and cut-out points, and inspecting the check valve for backflow. If your villa uses a rooftop tank, I clean the interior, replace the float mechanism and verify the overflow pipe isn't recirculating dirty water. For filtration I size the cartridge to your actual flow rate, fit it, flush the system so the first glass tastes right, and hand over a short note on what was worn and what to monitor next.

Before booking, snap three photos on WhatsApp: the pump unit with its model plate visible, the pressure gauge reading while it runs, and the tank area if relevant. A ten-second video of the cycling sound helps too. Tell me your area — Canggu, Kerobokan, Nusa Dua, wherever — and whether the issue appeared after a storm or crept in slowly. That context lets me bring the correct cartridges, gaskets and tools so we sort it in one visit rather than two.

sections.h3: Small Habits That Protect Your System
sections.text: Once a month, open the filter housing and rinse the cartridge under running tap water; swap it out when flow visibly drops. Keep the pressure switch dry — a stray splash from pool cleaning can corrode the contacts within days. In brackish-well areas like Jimbaran or Kuta, run the pump for ten minutes each morning to stop sediment settling in the impeller. And before the wet season hits Ubud or Seminyak, have the rooftop-tank lid sealed properly so leaf debris doesn't clog the inlet pipe.

faq.q: My pump runs constantly but there's no water at the taps. What could it be?
faq.a: Most often it's a failed check valve letting water drain back into the well, or an air leak on the suction side. I'll isolate which one it is once I'm on site.

faq.q: Do you handle both electric pumps and gravity-fed tank systems?
faq.a: Yes — whether your villa in Uluwatu relies on a rooftop tank or a submersible well pump in Canggu, I service both setups including switches, floats and filters.

faq.q: How do I get a quote without calling?
faq.a: Send photos of the unit plus a brief description of the problem via WhatsApp and I'll come back with what I need to bring and a ballpark scope. Final pricing depends on the specific job.
